guia.what: A ⌘K-style command palette with fuzzy search over grouped actions, fully keyboard-navigable. It opens with `⌘/Ctrl + K` or from a button.
whenUse: The app has many actions and destinations, and you want fast, searchable access to all of them.
Your audience uses the keyboard and values getting anywhere without the mouse.
You want one place to navigate and run actions instead of hunting for buttons.
whenAvoid: It’s a few actions on a specific trigger → `menu`.
You’re capturing a form value, not running commands → `combobox`.
The actions apply to an element and open with a right-click → `context-menu`.
dos: Group the commands and write good labels. That’s what gets filtered.
Also offer a visible path (a ⌘K button) so people can discover it.
donts: Don’t make it the only way in. Not everyone knows ⌘K exists.
Don’t put destructive commands behind a quick match without a confirmation.

nucleo: It combines a global keyboard shortcut, filtering, and focus. A global keyboard shortcut, filtering, and list navigation. Home and End move the caret in the input. It’s built on a modal `<dialog>`, so a single Esc press closes it. The “no results” text comes from a template in `data-ts-empty-for`.
